title: Final object and fibre products give finite limits, and functors preserving them preserve finite limits
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be categories, and assume $\mathcal C$ has a final object and fibre products. Then: (1) $\mathcal C$ has finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]; (2) let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor which carries every final object of $\mathcal C$ to a final object of $\mathcal D$ and every fibre product square of $\mathcal C$ (a commutative square $P\to A$, $P\to B$, $A\to S$, $B\to S$ exhibiting $P$ as a fibre product $A\times_SB$) to a fibre product square of $\mathcal D$. Then $F$ preserves finite limits: for every finite category $\mathcal I$, every functor $M:\mathcal I\to\mathcal C$ and every limit cone $(L,(\lambda_i:L\to M(i))_{i})$ of $M$, the cone $(F(L),(F(\lambda_i))_i)$ is a limit cone of $F\circ M$ in $\mathcal D$.

source.place: Lemma 002O (lemma-finite-limits-exist) for (1); for (2) the same construction of finite limits from products and equalizers (Lemma 002N, lemma-limits-products-equalizers), which are built from the final object and fibre products, and are therefore carried to limits by $F$
